title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Issues Concerning Whether a Guaranty Contract Is Valid Where an Enterprise Branch Without Legal Person Status Serves as a Guarantor for a Party to an Economic Contract and How to Handle Disputes Arising Therefrom

articles.content_en: Article 1: 1. The guarantor of an economic contract shall be a citizen, enterprise legal person, or other economic organization that has the capacity to perform on behalf of or to compensate. If a branch of an enterprise legal person, without having the status of a legal person and without the capacity to perform on behalf of or to compensate, acts as the guarantor for a party to an economic contract, the guarantee contract shall be confirmed as null and void.

Article 2: 2. According to Article 61 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, if the invalid guaranty act of the guarantor causes economic loss to the creditor of the economic contract, the guarantor shall also bear corresponding liability for compensation.

Article 3: 3. If a branch of an enterprise legal person does not have the capacity to perform on behalf of or to compensate, the enterprise legal person shall be listed as a litigation party in the lawsuit concerning the guaranty liability and shall bear the civil liability that the guarantor shall bear.
The specific cases involved in the request for instructions and report of your court shall be handled in accordance with the above principles.
Hereby reply.
March 24, 1988
